_comment: Cerebras WSE-3 (CS-3) single-wafer HAT twin. NO HBM - wafer-scale on-chip SRAM is the backing tier. RB-05: backing(44GB on-wafer SRAM)->reuse(48KB per-core local SRAM)->compute(dataflow-triggered FMAC PE). Single accelerator = 1 wafer = 900,000 cores. Sources: Cerebras WSE-3 press release + chip page + architecture deep-dive + Hot Chips 2024 + Tom's Hardware + arXiv 2503.11698. Reconciled from 1 authoring pass + 2 adversarial verifiers.
arch_note: no HBM; wafer-scale SRAM backing tier; all model state on-wafer resident. There is NO HBM spill cliff - state stays on-chip. This is the core contrast result, not a defect.

provenance.source: cerebras.ai press release + chip page + arXiv 2503.11698 + Tom's Hardware; 44GB @ 21PB/s confirmed by both verifiers. energy_pj_per_byte=1.0 is a generic on-chip-SRAM estimate (BRONZE, not published).

Cerebras deep-dive: 48KB/core over 8 single-ported 32-bit banks; 44GB/900k=48.9KB (even-division). per-core BW = 21PB/s / 900k = 23.3 GB/s, consistent with two 64-bit reads + one 64-bit write @1.1GHz.

device peak = 125 PFLOPS FP16 (GOLD; Cerebras press + Tom's Hardware) / 900k cores / 2 = 6.944e10 MAC/s per core, back-derived for twin self-consistency. matrix_unit [1,1,8] = 8-wide FP16 SIMD FMAC lane per both verifiers (WSE-3 = 2x WSE-2's 4-wide; researcher's [1,1,4] was WSE-2-era) - BRONZE, a dataflow SIMD lane not a systolic tile. clock 1.1GHz is BRONZE (Cerebras does not publish WSE-3 clock). NOTE: neither 4- nor 8-wide @1.1GHz reconciles with the 125 PFLOPS top-line (implies ~63 MAC/cycle/core) - see unresolved.

meta.tdp_note: ~23kW is full CS-3 15U SYSTEM power incl cooling/IO/host, NOT wafer die alone (BRONZE; wafer-only power undisclosed)
meta.fabric_note: ~214 Pb/s = 26.75 PB/s on-wafer 2D-mesh fabric (partly WSE-2-era); not a load-bearing tier for the single-device twin
